title: Flat, finitely presented, separated, quasi-finite morphisms are finite locally free on a stratification (Stacks 07RZ)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Then there exist closed subsets $\emptyset=Z_{-1}\subseteq Z_0\subseteq Z_1\subseteq Z_2\subseteq\cdots\subseteq S$ such that, with $S_r=Z_r\setminus Z_{r-1}$ ($r\geq0$), the sets $S_r$ are pairwise disjoint with union $S=\coprod_{r\ge0}S_r$, and this stratification has the following universal property: for every morphism of schemes $g:T\to S$, the projection $X\times_ST\to T$ (fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]) is finite locally free of degree $r$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free] if and only if $g(T)\subseteq S_r$ (as sets). Moreover, each inclusion $S_r\to S$ is quasi-compact, i.e. $S_r\cap W$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $W\subseteq S$. (Stacks Project, More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RZ.)

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RZ (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-qf), line 12845, with its proof (uses Morphisms Lemma 03JA and More on Morphisms Lemma 07RY)

proof.text: *Restriction to an affine open.* Let $W\subseteq S$ be an affine open, $X_W:=f^{-1}(W)$ and $f_W:=f|_{X_W}:X_W\to W$; by [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] $f_W$ is the base change of $f$ along the inclusion $W\to S$, and for every $s\in W$ its fibre $X_W\times_W\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ (pasting of the two cartesian squares, [def-pc-fibre-product]). As a base change, $f_W$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and locally of finite presentation [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (3). Since $f$ is quasi-finite, it is of finite type and every point of $X$ is isolated in its fibre [pqf-def-quasifinite]; $f$ is also separated, so the base change $f_W$ is separated and of finite type [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], and every point of $X_W$ is isolated in its fibre [lem-weil-pbc-isolated-fibre-point-base-change] (applied to $f$, which is locally of finite type, and $g:W\to S$). Hence $f_W$ is quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], in particular locally quasi-finite [pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc]. Finally $X_W=f^{-1}(W)$ is quasi-compact, because $f$ is quasi-compact (finite type, [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]) and $W$ is an affine open. By [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-qc-source-bounded-fibres] applied to $f_W$ there is an integer $n_W\ge0$ bounding the degrees of all fibres $X_s$, $s\in W$: each is a finite $\kappa(s)$-scheme of degree $\le n_W$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RZ (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-qf), proof, first paragraph ('The question is local on S, hence we may assume that S is affine. By Morphisms, Lemma 03JA the fibres of f are universally bounded in this case. Hence the existence of the stratification follows from Lemma 07RY'), the locality written out

proof.text: *The stratification over an affine open.* For each affine open $W\subseteq S$, step 1 shows that $f_W:X_W\to W$ satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-fp-lqf-bounded-stratification] with bound $n_W$. It gives closed subsets $\emptyset=Z^W_{-1}\subseteq Z^W_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq Z^W_{n_W}=W$ of $W$; put $Z^W_r:=W$ for $r>n_W$, $S^W_r:=Z^W_r\setminus Z^W_{r-1}$ for $r\ge0$ (so $S^W_r=\emptyset$ for $r>n_W$). The $S^W_r$ are pairwise disjoint with union $W$, $Z^W_r=S^W_0\cup\cdots\cup S^W_r$ for every $r\ge-1$ (induction on $r$ from $Z^W_{-1}=\emptyset$), and for every morphism $h:T\to W$ and $r\ge0$: $X_W\times_WT\to T$ is finite locally free of degree $r$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free] iff $h(T)\subseteq S^W_r$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RZ (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-qf), proof, first paragraph ('The question is local on S, hence we may assume that S is affine. By Morphisms, Lemma 03JA the fibres of f are universally bounded in this case. Hence the existence of the stratification follows from Lemma 07RY'), the locality written out

proof.text: *The strata are determined pointwise.* For $r\ge0$ define $S_r\subseteq S$ as the set of $s\in S$ such that the fibre $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is finite locally free of degree $r$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Claim: $S_r\cap W=S^W_r$ for every affine open $W$. Let $s\in W$; the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ has image $\{s\}\subseteq W$, so it factors through $W$ as $h_s:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to W$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme], and $X_W\times_W\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)=X_s$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ (step 1). By the universal property of step 2 applied to $h_s$, $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is finite locally free of degree $r$ iff $\{s\}\subseteq S^W_r$, i.e. $s\in S_r$ iff $s\in S^W_r$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RZ (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-qf), proof, first paragraph ('The question is local on S, hence we may assume that S is affine. By Morphisms, Lemma 03JA the fibres of f are universally bounded in this case. Hence the existence of the stratification follows from Lemma 07RY'), the locality written out

proof.text: *The closed subsets $Z_r$.* Put $Z_{-1}:=\emptyset$ and $Z_r:=S_0\cup\cdots\cup S_r$ for $r\ge0$; then $Z_{-1}\subseteq Z_0\subseteq Z_1\subseteq\cdots$. The affine opens $W$ cover $S$ [def-pc-scheme]. By steps 2 and 3, for each affine open $W$ the sets $S_r\cap W=S^W_r$ are pairwise disjoint with union $W$; since every point of $S$ lies in some $W$, the $S_r$ ($r\ge0$) are pairwise disjoint with union $S$, and hence $S_r=Z_r\setminus Z_{r-1}$. Moreover $Z_r\cap W=S^W_0\cup\cdots\cup S^W_r=Z^W_r$ is closed in $W$ (step 2). A subset whose intersection with every member of an open cover is closed in that member is closed (its complement is the union of the open sets $W\setminus(Z_r\cap W)$), so every $Z_r$ is closed in $S$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RZ (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-qf), proof, first paragraph ('The question is local on S, hence we may assume that S is affine. By Morphisms, Lemma 03JA the fibres of f are universally bounded in this case. Hence the existence of the stratification follows from Lemma 07RY'), the locality written out

proof.text: *Finite local freeness of degree $r$ is local on the target.* Let $h:Y\to T$ be a morphism of schemes, $r\ge0$, and $T=\bigcup_jT_j$ an open covering; write $h_j:Y_j:=h^{-1}(T_j)\to T_j$, which is the base change of $h$ along $T_j\to T$ [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product]. Then $h$ is finite locally free of degree $r$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free] iff every $h_j$ is. Indeed: (finite) $h$ is finite iff all $h_j$ are [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target] ((1)$\Leftrightarrow$(3) and the last sentence). (flat) The local rings $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $\mathcal O_{T,h(y)}$ and the map between them are the same for $h_j$ and $h$ when $y\in Y_j$, and every $y$ lies in some $Y_j$, so flatness of $h$ is flatness of all $h_j$ [def-weil-flat-morphism]. (locally of finite presentation) If $h$ is, so is each base change $h_j$ [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (3); conversely if all $h_j$ are, then for $y\in Y_j$ the affine opens $U\subseteq Y_j$, $V\subseteq T_j$ with $h(U)\subseteq V$ and $\mathcal O(V)\to\mathcal O(U)$ of finite presentation given by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] for $h_j$ are affine opens of $Y$, $T$, so $h$ is of finite presentation at $y$. (degree) For $t\in T_j$ (residue field $\kappa(t)$ the same in $T_j$ and $T$, [def-weil-residue-field]), the fibre $Y_j\times_{T_j}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is $Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ by pasting the cartesian square of [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] with the fibre square [def-pc-fibre-product]; so $\dim_{\kappa(t)}\Gamma$ of the fibre is the same for $h$ and $h_j$, and every $t$ lies in some $T_j$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RZ (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-qf), proof, first paragraph ('The question is local on S, hence we may assume that S is affine. By Morphisms, Lemma 03JA the fibres of f are universally bounded in this case. Hence the existence of the stratification follows from Lemma 07RY'), the locality written out

proof.text: *The universal property.* Let $g:T\to S$ be a morphism and $r\ge0$. For each affine open $W\subseteq S$ let $T_W:=g^{-1}(W)$ and $g_W:T_W\to W$ the restriction [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]; the $T_W$ form an open covering of $T$. The preimage of $T_W$ in $X\times_ST$ is $(X\times_ST)\times_TT_W=X\times_ST_W=X_W\times_WT_W$ over $T_W$, by [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] (twice) and pasting of cartesian squares [def-pc-fibre-product]. By step 5, $X\times_ST\to T$ is finite locally free of degree $r$ iff for every affine open $W$ the projection $X_W\times_WT_W\to T_W$ is; by the universal property of step 2 (for $f_W$ and $g_W$) this holds iff $g(T_W)\subseteq S^W_r=S_r\cap W$ (step 3) for every $W$; since $T=\bigcup_WT_W$ and $g(T_W)\subseteq W$, this is equivalent to $g(T)\subseteq S_r$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RZ (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-qf), proof, first paragraph ('The question is local on S, hence we may assume that S is affine. By Morphisms, Lemma 03JA the fibres of f are universally bounded in this case. Hence the existence of the stratification follows from Lemma 07RY'), the locality written out

proof.text: *Quasi-compactness, set-up.* For $r\ge-1$ put $U_r:=S\setminus Z_r$, open by step 4, with $U_{-1}=S\supseteq U_0\supseteq U_1\supseteq\cdots$ and $Z_r\cap U_{r-1}=Z_r\setminus Z_{r-1}=S_r$ for $r\ge0$. Fix $r\ge0$ and an affine open $W'=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq U_{r-1}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $Z_r\cap W'=S_r\cap W'$ is closed in $W'$, hence of the form $V(I)$ for an ideal $I\subseteq A$ (definition of the Zariski topology). The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ induced by the surjection $A\to A/I$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] (2) [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose image is $V(I)$ (the primes of $A/I$ are the $\mathfrak p/I$ with $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$). Composing with the inclusion $W'\to S$ gives $g:\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to S$ with $g(\operatorname{Spec}(A/I))=V(I)\subseteq S_r$, so by step 6 the projection $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ is finite locally free of degree $r$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RZ (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-qf), proof, second paragraph (quasi-compactness of U_r = S minus Z_r)

proof.text: *Descending to a finitely generated ideal.* Let $\Lambda$ be the set of finitely generated ideals $I_\lambda\subseteq I$, directed by inclusion; $I=\bigcup_\lambda I_\lambda$, so $A/I=\varinjlim_\lambda A/I_\lambda$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)=\varprojlim_\lambda\operatorname{Spec}(A/I_\lambda)$ with affine transition morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite-locally-free] with $S_0=Y_0=W'$, $S_\lambda=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I_\lambda)$ (index $0$ the ideal $(0)$) and $f_0=f_{W'}:X_{W'}\to W'$: here $W'$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated; $X_{W'}$ is quasi-compact (step 1) and quasi-separated since $f_{W'}$ is separated over the affine $W'$ [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine]; $f_{W'}$ is locally of finite presentation (step 1). Its base change to $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ is $X_{W'}\times_{W'}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ (pasting with [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product], [def-pc-fibre-product]), finite locally free of degree $r$ by step 7. Hence there is $\lambda$ with $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}(A/I_\lambda)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/I_\lambda)$ finite locally free of degree $r$, and by step 6 the image $V(I_\lambda)$ of $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I_\lambda)\to S$ (step 7 for $I_\lambda$) lies in $S_r\cap W'=V(I)$. As $I_\lambda\subseteq I$, also $V(I)\subseteq V(I_\lambda)$; so $Z_r\cap W'=V(I_\lambda)=V(a_1,\ldots,a_m)$ for generators $a_1,\ldots,a_m$ of $I_\lambda$, and $U_r\cap W'=W'\setminus V(I_\lambda)=D(a_1)\cup\cdots\cup D(a_m)$. Each $D(a_k)\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_{a_k}$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] (iii), so $U_r\cap W'$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RZ (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-qf), proof, second paragraph (quasi-compactness of U_r = S minus Z_r)

proof.text: *$U_r\to S$ is quasi-compact.* Claim: for every affine open $W\subseteq S$ and every $r\ge-1$, $U_r\cap W$ is quasi-compact. Induction on $r$: $U_{-1}\cap W=W$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] (iii). For $r\ge0$, the open $U_{r-1}\cap W$ is quasi-compact by induction, so it is covered by finitely many affine opens $W'_1,\ldots,W'_m\subseteq U_{r-1}\cap W$ (affine opens form a basis [def-pc-scheme]); since $U_r\subseteq U_{r-1}$, $U_r\cap W=\bigcup_k(U_r\cap W'_k)$, a finite union of quasi-compact sets by step 8, hence quasi-compact. (This is Stacks' 'composition of the quasi-compact maps $U_r\to U_{r-1}$'.)

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RZ (lemma-stratify-flat-fp-qf), proof, second paragraph (quasi-compactness of U_r = S minus Z_r)

proof.text: *$S_r\to S$ is quasi-compact.* Let $W\subseteq S$ be a quasi-compact open and $r\ge0$; $W$ is a finite union of affine opens $W_1,\ldots,W_m$ [def-pc-scheme]. For each $k$, $S_r\cap W_k=Z_r\cap(U_{r-1}\cap W_k)$ (step 7) is a closed subset of $U_{r-1}\cap W_k$, which is quasi-compact by step 9; a closed subset of a quasi-compact space is quasi-compact. Hence $S_r\cap W=\bigcup_k(S_r\cap W_k)$ is quasi-compact. Together with steps 4 and 6 this proves the statement.

split_report.summary: Statement checked against Stacks 07RZ (more-morphisms.tex line 12845) and kept. Proof follows the two paragraphs of the Stacks proof in ten steps. First paragraph ('local on S; 03JA; 07RY'): restriction of f to an affine open W is again flat, lfp, separated, quasi-finite with quasi-compact source, so its fibres are universally bounded (existing node 03JA); 07RY (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-flat-fp-lqf-bounded-stratification, stated with the 03J4 bound inline and S_r empty for r > n) stratifies W; the gluing that Stacks leaves implicit is written out: the strata are characterized pointwise by the universal property at Spec kappa(s), so they agree on overlaps, Z_r is closed because it is closed in every affine open, and the universal property is checked on the cover g^{-1}(W) using that finite local freeness of degree r is local on the target (step 5, from the existing finite/flat/lfp nodes). Second paragraph (quasi-compactness): for an affine W' in U_{r-1}, Z_r cap W' = V(I) and V(I) = V(I_lambda) for a finitely generated I_lambda via Limits 06AC (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite-locally-free) applied to the limit Spec(A/I) = lim Spec(A/I_lambda); then U_r cap W is quasi-compact by induction, and S_r cap W is closed in the quasi-compact U_{r-1} cap W. Tags 07RY, 07RZ, 03J4, 03JA, 06AC verified in tags/tags. lean.statement: theorem exists_closed_stratification_of_flat_quasiFinite {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [IsSeparated f] (hf : f.IsQuasiFinite) : ∃ Z : ℕ → Set S, Z 0 = ∅ ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, IsClosed (Z n)) ∧ Monotone Z ∧ Pairwise (fun r t : ℕ => Disjoint (Z (r + 1) \ Z r) (Z (t + 1) \ Z t)) ∧ (⋃ r : ℕ, Z (r + 1) \ Z r) = Set.univ ∧ (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : T ⟶ S) (r : ℕ), (pullback.snd f g).IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree r ↔ Set.range g ⊆ Z (r + 1) \ Z r) ∧ (∀ (r : ℕ) (W : S.Opens), IsCompact (W : Set S) → IsCompact ((Z (r + 1) \ Z r) ∩ (W : Set S)))
